summary:
Patient Overview
Pervaiz Akhtar, a 74-year-old retired male with significant family history of diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease, presents with lower extremity edema and proteinuria. Current medications include Bisoprolol for blood pressure control and Budesonide/Formoterol for asthma management.

Key Findings
• Significant proteinuria (+++) and mucosuria (+++) on urine routine examination (14-JUN-2025)
• Serum chemistry panel shows normal liver and kidney function parameters
• eGFR at 67.56 mL/min/1.73 m² (borderline but within acceptable range for age)
• Blood pressure 130/87 mmHg, slightly elevated despite medication
• Heart rate 92 bpm, slightly tachycardic
• Borderline diabetic status requiring close monitoring
• Physical examination shows swelling in lower shanks and feet

Risk Assessment
Moderate to high risk for diabetic or hypertensive nephropathy given significant proteinuria, family history, and current comorbidities. Age and cardiovascular risk factors increase likelihood of renal disease progression. Peripheral edema suggests possible early heart failure or advanced kidney involvement. Urgent need for comprehensive renal assessment and optimization of blood pressure and glucose control.

Recommendations
• Obtain spot urine protein/creatinine ratio (UPCR) to quantify proteinuria severity
• Initiate diuretic therapy to manage peripheral edema and fluid retention
• Add ACE inhibitor or ARB for renoprotection and improved blood pressure control
• Comprehensive metabolic panel and HbA1c to assess diabetes status
• Monitor weight daily to track fluid retention
• Elevate feet above heart level when resting
• Nephrology referral for proteinuria evaluation and management
• Continue Bisoprolol and Budesonide/Formoterol as prescribed
• Close monitoring of kidney function with regular follow-up visits
• Dietary sodium restriction and fluid intake monitoring
